result.details:
Checkout: disposable detached clone /tmp/opencode/r16/repo at d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (git rev-parse HEAD verified); /workspace/repo untouched and clean at baseline 5672ead2a526e07fea9ed11e58b3725e42013527. Toolchain: snapshot bun 1.3.14 refuses bun.lock lockfileVersion 2, so official Bun 1.4.2 was unpacked to /tmp/opencode/bun142 and used for install and tests; the lockfile was never rewritten (bun install --frozen-lockfile exit 0).

What I verified as correct (no finding): acquireProcessLock is a real advisory flock (src/runtime.ts:106-135, :145-171) with O_NOFOLLOW, 0600, mkdir of the parent at 0700, a namedHandle dev/ino re-check that retries up to 8 times so an unlink/recreate race cannot yield two owners on one inode, and an unlink guarded by the same dev/ino check before LOCK_UN/close. Ownership order in src/serve.ts: :121-122 refuses :memory:, :126 derives the lock from the DB path, :161 lock before :162 SQLite, :163-166 persisted instance_id check, :140-157 reverse-ordered idempotent release (shutdown memoized via releasing ??= release()) with SQLite closed before the lock is released. Coordinator.stop can only wait (src/coordinator.ts:260-300, the idle promise is always resolved by wakeIdle), so a rollback cannot reject and mask the original startup error. scripts/smoke.ts:19 also takes the lock before opening SQLite; status/config are HTTP or read-only and never take it. Confirmed empirically: crash/SIGKILL stale lock recovered; stale lock containing a live unrelated PID acquired successfully; a refused contender leaves the owner's PID content and mtime unchanged; 5-way simultaneous acquire leaves exactly one owner; port conflict, failed recovery and foreign instance_id all release lock, SQLite handles and both ports; SQLite -wal/-shm sidecars are 0600 even when the parent directory pre-exists 0755, so no local disclosure via sidecars; a file:-shaped DB path is treated by Bun as a literal filename, so no URI/lock desync.

Findings (3 LOW) are detailed in /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/findings.json and review.md: (1) src/serve.ts:126 lock identity follows the configured path string rather than the database file, so a symlink/hardlink/bind-mount alias of one DB takes a separate lock and the instance_id guard is inert under the default instance ID - reproduced in /tmp/opencode/r16/probes/ownership.ts (alias ACQUIRED, rows cross-visible; symlinked-directory control REFUSED); recommend canonicalising the parent path or recording the DB dev/ino in the lock file; (2) src/runtime.ts:153 refusal message omits the lock path and holder PID that src/runtime.ts:160 already records; (3) docs/SERVE.md:40 and :48 invert the listener/log-interval order versus src/serve.ts:141-146 (documentation only; tests assert effects, not order).

Limitations: scope-limited (no full-suite run, no compile/packaging step); no real cloud or model provider contacted - fake provider/agent doubles only; finding 1 demonstrated at the lock+SQLite layer rather than with two live startServer instances; flock behaviour on NFS/FUSE/overlayfs could not be exercised and a silent no-op flock there is an unverified hypothesis, deliberately not reported as a finding (docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:61 already requires a persistent local volume). No secret files inspected; no credentials in any output. Probes live only in /tmp/opencode/r16/probes, logs in /workspace/.swarmforge/logs.
